conviction_note: Six small findings net +0.3. The Q2 dividend was declared after the quarter closed, Jun-Aug loan marks were flat, and forward base rates are 42bp higher; against that sit a 6%-to-8% refinancing, a bar that needs a sequential NII rise after a 16% miss, and a CFO exit. I emit +0.2, a tenth below the sum, because this name has fallen after 6 of its last 7 prints (mean -4.6%) and paid only +1.55% for its one in-line print; that reaction history vetoes most of the positive read.
bar: Adjusted NII $0.49/share, revenue $31.47M for the quarter ended 2026-08-31 (MarketBeat family, via https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/09/29/saratoga-investment-sar-set-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday.html, snippet_only, page 403). One other aggregator snippet showed $0.54, likely stale. There are not two agreeing independent sources and no company guide, so every finding is capped small. FY27 EPS consensus $1.94 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/dividend-saratoga-investment-corp-nyse-sar-declares-monthly-dividend-of-025-2026-09-09/) less Q1's $0.47 implies about $0.49/quarter, which agrees with the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest is snippet_only and the sources disagree: 593K shares, 3.65% of float, 6.69 days to cover (Barchart-type snippet) against 197,619 shares, 1.49% of float, 1.9 days (Fintel, https://fintel.io/ss/us/sar, page 403). Both are search snippets seen 2026-10-01. Either way it is not a crowded short. There is no usable option chain (total OI 0), so no skew. Institutional ownership is 19%, so holders are mostly retail yield buyers. The stock is at its 52-week low, -9.2% over 20 days, and trades at 0.72x the May NAV of $23.23.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09, after the Q2 quarter closed on 08-31, the board kept the $0.75 Q3 FY27 dividend ($0.25 monthly) 'carefully considering current and expected earnings levels, portfolio dynamics and our spillover position'. So the 10-06 release cannot carry the dividend cut that a 63%-covered payout invites, which removes the main tail behind the -14% July reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no dividend cut in the 7-print history. The July 2026 print (-14.09%) came with the CEO saying it was 'too early to make a hard call on a dividend change', so the reaction priced cut risk.
findings.why_not_priced: Since the declaration the stock has fallen from $17.64 (09-04) to $16.66 at an 18% yield. If the market believed the payout was safe through November, the yield would not be widening into the print. The call (10-07, 10:00 ET) can still bring dividend commentary, which is why the low end is negative.
findings.independence: The CEO's July call said there are about 5 quarters of spillover (about $1.50/share) at the current payout (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-saratoga-investment-misses-q1-2026-estimates-as-stock-falls-93CH-4782007). That is a different document.

findings.finding: Loan-market marks were flat across SAR's Jun-Aug quarter, unlike Q1 when software loans were still selling off. Performing software loans went from 87.71 at end-May to 87.73 at end-Aug, non-software from 96.80 to 97.06, and the index returned +0.79% in July and +0.93% in August. Market-driven unrealized depreciation should be far below Q1's $0.93/share, leaving NAV roughly $23.23 less about $0.27 of under-earning plus idiosyncratic marks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NAV down 4.9% in July 2026 brought a -14.09% reaction. FY26 NAV erosion from $25.86 to $24.42 came with -3.1% (May 2026). A smaller NAV drop has not been tested as a positive.
findings.why_not_priced: At 0.72x the May NAV, and with the discount widening into the print, the price implies continued NAV erosion. If the flat-marks quarter were priced, the discount would have narrowed with the July-August loan rally, and it widened instead.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: broadly syndicated (BSL) index prices, not SAR's own Level 3 marks. The end-May software level comes from a separate PitchBook May wrap (https://pitchbook.com/news/reports/may-2026-us-leveraged-loan-index-monthly-wrap) and the end-June low of 85.65 from the July wrap (https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/july-wrap-software-insurance-sectors-lead-loan-rally). Counterweight, netted into the size: Exigo is marked at 70% of cost with 'some principal definitely at risk' and Chronus has maturity concerns (July call transcript).

findings.finding: 3M term SOFR is 4.083% on 2026-09-30 against 3.66% on 2026-05-31 (10-Q). The Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 and the dot plot shows another hike. SAR's book is predominantly floating 1M/3M SOFR loans, and the September notes repaid a floating SPV facility, so forward NII rises by roughly $0.03-0.05/quarter. The 10-07 call can present this as closing the dividend gap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SAR does not issue formal guidance. In FY26 falling rates were the stated driver of NII declines, alongside reactions of -4.71%, -7.94% and -2.88%. A rate tailwind has not been tested in this history.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell about 4% from the 09-16 hike to 09-30 while its floating-rate earnings base repriced up about 42bp. If the market were crediting the NII lift, coverage-driven names like SAR would have firmed after the hike rather than making new lows.
findings.independence: The Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% is in a different source (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html, snippet). The 3.66% end-May base and floating-rate structure are in the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1377936/000121390026075931/ea0295366-10q_saratoga.htm). The size is inference: the company has not quantified the effect since the hike.

findings.finding: SAR refinanced its $105.5M 6.00% Notes due 2027 with $120.8M of 8.00% Notes due 2031: $85M priced 08-18 and closed 08-26, with reopenings on 09-02 and 09-23. The ~$23M from the 09-23 tranche went to repay the Valley National SPV facility. That is about 200bp more on ~$105M (about -$0.025/quarter of NII after incentive fee), plus a month of double carry into Q3. It offsets most of the rate tailwind in forward run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Higher unsecured borrowing cost was cited as a driver of the Q1 NII decline (BDC Reporter, July 2026), which came with a -14.09% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The rule-4 question is what the money buys. It buys a refinancing of a 2027 maturity at a higher coupon, not a deployment ramp, so the sign is negative but it is a cost, not distress. The issue is public and probably modeled, which is why the size is small. It reaches the price through Q3 run-rate commentary on the call.
findings.independence: The size and the use of the 09-23 tranche come from the 8-K filed 2026-09-24 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1377936/000121390026103054/ea0306545-8k_saratoga.htm), the same financing seen in a second document.

findings.finding: The $0.49 bar needs about 4% sequential NII growth from Q1's $0.47, which itself missed $0.5585 by 16%. Post-quarter activity disclosed in July was only +$16M net in June ($47M of follow-ons against $31M of repayments). Exigo ($17.1M fair value, $24.8M cost) is on the red watchlist and Saratoga CLO interest income is already $0.0, so a small miss or in-line print is more likely than a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII misses: -14.09% (Jul 2026, -16%) and -4.71% (Oct 2025, miss). The in-line print of May 2026 drew -3.1%, and the one up move (+1.55%, Jan 2026) followed a $0.61 quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still models improvement (revenue $31.47M against Q1's $30.78M) on a name that has missed or matched on recent prints. If the market expected a miss, the bar would sit at or below $0.47.
findings.independence: Exigo and Chronus cost and fair value are in the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1377936/000121390026075931/ea0295366-10q_saratoga.htm), and CLO interest of $0.0 is in the 10-K/10-Q search snippet. Netted: deploying Q1's $60.8M cash (up from $21.8M) is the offsetting tailwind and is why the size is small.

findings.finding: CFO Henri Steenkamp is stepping down effective 2026-10-31 for health reasons (8-K, 2026-09-18), with no disagreement. The Controller becomes principal financial officer. The 10-07 call is his last as CFO.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no precedent in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since it was public 18 days before the print. The residual is the call-day risk of questions on continuity when the CFO and the dividend-coverage story change hands at the same time.
findings.independence: Press release of the same date (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/18/3364940/0/en/saratoga-investment-corp-announces-cfo-transition-and-new-leadership-appointments.html). It is the same event in a second document.

outside_window.finding: The Q4 FY27 dividend decision (Dec-Feb payments) is the real cut catalyst. The board declares quarterly around early-to-mid of the quarter's second month; the Q3 declaration came 09-09. With coverage at about 63% and spillover falling about $0.25/quarter, a cut is the main medium-term risk, and it is not decided in this window.
Q3 FY27 will carry about a month of double interest on the 8% 2031 notes before the 6% 2027 notes are redeemed, plus the full step-up. This lands in the January 2027 print.

searched_and_found_nothing: Event check: the company release (globenewswire 2026-09-17) confirms results 2026-10-06 after the close and the call 2026-10-07 at 10:00 ET.

EDGAR filings since 2026-06-01: 10-Q 07-07; 8-K 5.07 on 09-23 (directors and auditor only, no below-NAV issuance authority sought); 8-K 1.01/2.03 notes on 09-24; 8-K CFO on 09-18. No Item 2.02 pre-release, no non-reliance, no subsequent-event 8-K on portfolio companies.

Portfolio-company news for Exigo, Chronus and Pepper Palace: no 2026 restructuring, sale or default news found.
Saratoga CLO 2013-1: in wind-down, interest income already $0.0 and mgmt fee $0.5M in Q1, so it is already in the run-rate.
BDC sector context (BIZD, Fitch 'deteriorating' outlook): generic, nothing company-specific.
Consensus pages (Zacks, Nasdaq, TradingKey) were blocked or blank, so the bar rests on MarketBeat-family snippets.
Options: the chain is unusable (0 OI), so there is no skew to read.
Hiring, app or web alternative series: not meaningful for a ~$270M externally managed BDC. Loan-market price series and term SOFR were used as the alternative series instead.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive and agree with the 20-day run-up of -9.2% (no skew exists), but the name's own reaction history is strongly negative (6 of 7 down, mean -4.6%). I give the history the final say: the emitted +0.2 is below the +0.3 findings sum.
lessons_applied: Rule 6: the bar has one source family, not two agreeing sources, so every finding stays capped small. The largest is 0.6, so nothing was raised.
Rule 5: the loan-mark finding is a broadly syndicated index proxy, not SAR's own Level 3 marks, so it was cut from +0.5 to +0.4, with independence saying it is a proxy.
Rule 5: the SOFR-to-NII transmission is not quantified by the company since the hike, so it was cut from +0.6 to +0.4.
Rule 4: I asked what the refinancing buys. It refinances a 2027 maturity at +200bp; it is not distress and not a ramp, so it was cut from -0.5 to -0.4 and the sign kept.
Rules 1 and 3: the reaction history (6 of 7 down) kept the emitted move below the sum, +0.2 against +0.3.
Rule 7: I checked short interest before the negatives (1.5-3.7% of float, not crowded), so no squeeze haircut was needed.
Left standing: the dividend finding (+0.6), the NII-bar finding (-0.5), the CFO finding (-0.2) and print_vs_bar (-2.0).
